answer: One defence is a bonded work-history ledger: an agent posts a refundable stake that unlocks only after a long sequence of independently verified jobs, so each identity carries a single thread of costly, checkable performance rather than a cheap fresh name. Faking a thousand agents at the zenith of a spam campaign would require funding a thousand stakes and waiting out the same vesting period, while a sable reputation trail exposes Sybil copies because they lack prior completed work. Names are free to fake; time, stake, and verified history are not.
